items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: We had a guest, Bob Dorough and Jon Gordon the alto player, the young alto player. And so we were doing this gig

ctx.x: I’ve often wondered about that. Sometimes you see a record where it’s a quartet except for one song that’s a trio. Like no chordal instrument. And you think, “Oh that was very experimental for them” when in fact probably the piano player just couldn’t finish.

Or really more esperential. Yeah it happens. Those are scenes where you get prepared to do a recording. I like to do live recordings a lot and there was one we were going to do in New York at a club with Phil and I had it all set up. We had a really great relationship with Bruce Lundvall in these last years when he was at Blue Note. We became very © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

friendly over the years and I wanted to do a — we had done — I’d done some records for Bruce for Blue Note but I hadn’t done Phil’s group. I said you know we could do something with Phil. And he said that maybe that was a good idea but he didn’t know. So then we were going to do a thing at this club in New York called The Iridium and we were going to have the quintet with Brian Lynch, Phil, and Bill Charlap, Steve Gilmore and myself.
